newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.12 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.12 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 1.12 percent on Wednesday in continued selective activity as the market overcame resistance at 1,170, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,178, up 13 points from Tuesday's previous record of 1,165. In dollar terms, it rose to a record of $1.05 from Tuesday's $1.04.
Trade volume dropped to 20.17 trillion lira from 21.14 trillion on Tuesday.
"The market continues its uptrend with intermittent profit-taking and share-based activity," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.

Two-day gains totalled 3.7 percent since Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the recent rally sparked by lower money and bond market rates, a quiet dollar and 1996 profit prospects of companies since the beginning of 1997.
The index had surged 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consecutive days after the market reopened on January 2, following a five-day holiday.

Of the 238 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 112 to 74 and 52 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.81 percent to 1,237, the IMKB Services eased 0.42 percent to 1,199 and the IMKB Finacial leapt 2.32 percent to 1,145.
Top actives were utility Aktas Elektrik, down 2,500 lira at 117,500 and motor vehicle producer Otosan, up 2,000 lira at 50,500. They made up 10.8 percent of the total turnover.
